# Intrinsic finite-base upper bound and exclusion of zero-depth locations

This extends the proved finite-base quantile upper bound to the intrinsic
Hausdorff measure in the task. It is an upper bound, not the required OC
lower bound. The finite affine-majorant lemma, including its closed-cone
proof, is in `candidate 4e07416b95553009`.

## 1. Measure and statement

Let C be a convex body in R^n times R^d, let S=C intersect (Z^n times R^d)
be nonempty, and let q=dim_H(S). The integer projection of S is finite.
For every nonempty fiber K_z=C_z, its Hausdorff dimension is its affine
dimension. Consequently q is the largest of these integer dimensions.
Let P be the set of bases of the q-dimensional fibers, and put N=|P|.
Every K_z for z in P has positive finite H_q measure, while every other
fiber has H_q measure zero. Finite additivity on the disjoint embedded
fibers gives

    H_q(S)=sum_(z in P) H_q(K_z),   0<H_q(S)<infinity.

For q>=1 and z in P, let f_z(y) be the ordinary raw halfspace depth of
y in K_z, computed in its q-dimensional affine hull with H_q. Let D_S
be the raw ambient mixed depth computed with H_q. Then

    D_S(z,y) <= N f_z(y).                              (1)

Every point lying in a fiber of dimension less than q has D_S=0. Every
point in the relative boundary of a q-dimensional fiber also has D_S=0.
Thus positive intrinsic depth can occur only in the relative interior
of a q-dimensional fiber. Such locations do exist: the centroid of any
q-dimensional fiber has positive raw depth from its own fiber alone.

For q=0, every nonempty fiber is a singleton, H_0 is counting measure,
and (1) reduces to the trivial bound D_S<=N with f_z=1. There are no
lower-dimensional nonempty fibers or relative-boundary points in this
case.

## 2. A lower-dimensional fiber has zero depth

Suppose dim(K_z0)<q. Its base z0 cannot belong to conv(P). Otherwise,
write z0 as a convex combination of bases in P, omitting zero weights.
The same Minkowski combination of their fibers is contained in K_z0
by actual convexity of C. It has affine dimension at least q: fixing
all but any one of its positive-weight q-dimensional summands already
exhibits a q-dimensional subset. This is a contradiction.

The finite compact convex set conv(P) can therefore be strictly
separated from z0. A purely integer-coordinate ambient closed halfspace
contains the whole z0 fiber and excludes every base in P. It captures
zero H_q mass, proving D_S=0. For n=0 such a lower-dimensional source
fiber cannot exist, so there is no nonexistent integer normal to use.

## 3. Generic continuous normals and intrinsic quantiles

Fix z0 in P, y in K_z0, and q>=1. Write E_z for the q-dimensional
direction space of K_z. The finite union of proper linear subspaces

    union_(z in P) E_z^perp

has empty interior in R^d. Thus any continuous vector can be
approximated by vectors u whose restriction to EVERY E_z is nonzero.
For such a u, all continuous cutting hyperplanes have zero H_q mass
in every positive-measure fiber. Its fiber tails are continuous and
strictly decreasing between their support levels.

Take a proper source level s and let

    t=H_q(K_z0 intersect {u.x>=s}),  0<t<H_q(K_z0).

For each z in P with H_q(K_z)>t choose its unique proper threshold h_z
capturing H_q volume t. The source is among these constrained bases
and h_z0=s. Other bases require no constraint: their whole mass is
already at most t.

The finite affine-majorant lemma applies as follows. Let nonnegative
weights on constrained bases have sum one and base barycenter z0.
Their captured-body Minkowski combination is contained in K_z0.
Every positive-weight captured body has dimension q. Its direction
space must be contained in E_z0: fix points in the other summands and
vary this one summand in the contained Minkowski combination. Both
spaces have dimension q, so E_z=E_z0 for EVERY positive-weight summand.
This proves the needed parallelism rather than assuming it for all
fibers in advance.

Translate these parallel affine hulls into E_z0. Translation preserves
their intrinsic H_q measures, and q-dimensional Brunn--Minkowski gives

    H_q(sum weights times captured bodies)^(1/q)
        >= sum weights times t^(1/q)=t^(1/q).

The combination lies above the threshold sum weights times h_z.
Since s is the proper source t-quantile, it follows that

    sum weights times h_z <= s.

The finite affine-majorant lemma therefore supplies b in R^n with

    h_z <= s+b.(z-z0)

for every constrained base. The single actual ambient halfspace

    H={ (z,x):u.x>=s+b.(z-z0) }

captures at most t in each positive-measure fiber. It has nonzero
continuous normal u and captures total H_q mass at most Nt. Fibers of
dimension less than q contribute zero; no boundary mass has been
discarded in the positive-measure fibers because of the generic choice
of u.

## 4. Pass only source cut volumes to the desired intrinsic direction

The source's intrinsic ordinary depth is attained on the unit sphere
of E_z0: the cap volume depends continuously on its normal there,
because its boundary is a proper lower-dimensional affine section or
a supporting section of zero H_q measure. Opposite through-point caps
sum to the source volume, so f_z0(y)<=H_q(K_z0)/2.

First suppose f_z0(y)>0. Extend a minimizing intrinsic normal u0 to
R^d, and choose generic u_l tending to u0. Source cap volumes at
s_l=u_l.y converge to f_z0(y) by dominated convergence, since u0 is
nonzero on E_z0 and its boundary has zero H_q measure. For large l
these volumes are positive and strictly less than the source volume.
Section 3 constructs actual containing halfspaces, through (z0,y),
with total masses at most N times these volumes. Taking the infimum
over containing halfspaces and then the limit proves (1). There is
no limit of selected points or of integer-coordinate normal vectors.

If f_z0(y)=0, use the same approximating generic normals but choose
source levels s_l=u_l.y-epsilon_l with epsilon_l>0 tending to zero.
They contain y strictly and have positive source cap volume. For large
l the volume is strictly subtotal and tends to zero by the same
dominated-convergence argument. Section 3 again gives containing caps
whose total masses tend to zero. Thus D_S=0. This avoids assuming an
attaining zero-mass ambient cap or bounded integer tilts.

A point in the relative boundary of K_z0 has ordinary depth zero,
by a supporting hyperplane in its affine hull. This proves the claimed
relative-boundary exclusion. For a relative interior centroid g,
ordinary q-dimensional Gruenbaum gives every containing ambient cap
at least Gamma_q H_q(K_z0) from its own fiber whenever its trace is
a genuine halfspace; a trace containing the whole fiber gives still
more. Thus D_S(z0,g)>0, proving the final existence assertion without
claiming the target OC fraction of the total mass.
